messages:
mira: Heads-up — after yesterday's batcher window increase we see repeated cudaMalloc spikes on the prod GPU pool. Started ~09:10 UTC, P95 latency blips and allocation rate up.
mira: quick summary: adaptive-window 32->64, model: redwood-7b-chat-v1, weight-quantized. No code change except batcher policy. Trace attached (nsys + arena snapshot).
danny: can you paste the nsys command you ran and a short kernel timeline snippet?
mira: nsys command I used:
```
nsys profile --output /tmp/nsys_run --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx --sample=cpu -t 60 --force true --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi -- ./run_load_test.sh
```
kernel timeline (abridged):
```
GPU time window 09:15:21-09:15:27
- allocate cudaMalloc  2.8ms  @ 09:15:21.143
- kernel matmul_v2    0.9ms
- cudaMemcpyAsync     0.4ms
- cudaMalloc          3.1ms @ 09:15:21.278
- kernel attn_kv      1.2ms
- cudnn conv          0.7ms
- cudaMalloc          2.5ms @ 09:15:21.391
```
perf-bot: alert: allocation_rate increased 3.8x vs baseline; memory_fragmentation_ratio=0.27 :rotating_light:
ken: hypothesis: expanding batch window raises peak concurrent sequence length variability. That increases KV cache churn — more evictions/re-hydrations -> many small allocations when we rebuild KV segments. Also kernel selection changed: for some seq len combos the runtime picked KV-merge kernels that allocate temporary buffers per stream.
olga: ran arena snapshot on a canary host. Script: `scripts/arena-snapshot.sh --pid <pid> --o /tmp/snap.json`
olga: excerpt from snapshot (humanized):
```
total_allocated: 28.7 GiB
total_free: 7.8 GiB
largest_free_chunk: 1.2 MiB
free_buckets: {64: 12k, 128: 9k, 256: 4k, 512: 600}
fragmentation_ratio: 0.32
per-stream_arena_counts: stream0: 1200 chunks, stream1: 900, stream2: 30
```
olga: note: huge skew in per-stream arenas — stream2 rarely used and its arena is mostly free, stream0/1 have lots of small free chunks.
mira: I flipped a canary to cudaMallocAsync + memory pool (cudaMemPool). Results: allocation count down 68%, P95 latency down ~18%. But we saw increased host pinned memory faults on one instance (hostalloc fallback).
sam_repo: pushed WIP PR that does two things: (1) reduce slab split threshold from 512 -> 256 to avoid splitting into lots of tiny chunks, (2) enable per-stream arena creation only on demand and cap arena growth to 128MB by default. bench script: `tools/run_membench.sh --iters 1000`.
sam_repo: quick bench numbers (short run):
```
baseline allocs/sec: 420
with cudaMallocAsync: 130
with slab-threshold 256 + per-stream-cap: allocs/sec: 170
end-to-end latency P95: baseline 148ms -> patched 135ms
```
danny: can you record a perfetto trace with the NVTX ranges around batcher decision and the KV eviction path? I want to correlate host-side allocation spikes with kernel timeline.
mira: yes — perfetto command I used:
```
perfetto -c perfetto_cfg.pbtxt -o /tmp/trace.perfetto
# cfg includes: track_cgroups, gpu_vms, custom nvtx slice names for batcher/kv
```
mira: uploaded short trace to the internal perf bucket: gs://redwood-perf/traces/1867004444-batcher-kv-1.perfetto
ken: actionable items I see:
- re-run canary with slab-threshold patch + cudaMallocAsync
- add per-request NVTX spans around KV rehydrate + mark when kernel selector flips to KV-merge
- add a microbenchmark that reproduces small-chunk churn (vary seq lengths 16-2048; batch sizes 1..64)
- check kernel selection heuristics for sequences near the boundary; maybe our kernel chooser prefers a kernel that allocates temporaries for certain seq combos
mira: repro steps I used (minimal):
```
# reproduce locally
# 1) run small harness that sends mixes of short/long sequences
python tools/send_mixed_seq.py --endpoint localhost:8080 --mix "short:80,long:20" --duration 120
# 2) profile with nsys as above + perfetto
```
mira: notes: when I force the kernel selector to the older path (env KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy) the alloc spikes disappear, but latency increases slightly. So it's a tradeoff.
danny: good. let's also add a long-run canary (6h) to catch slow fragmentation growth. If the slab patch holds, we can merge to canary and watch mem fragmentation metric + allocation_rate.
olga: I'll schedule the 6h canary tonight and collect hourly arena snapshots. Will paste results tomorrow.
mira: thanks all — saving traces and logs in the incident thread bucket: gs://redwood-incidents/1867004444/
sam_repo: I'll open the PR for review now and attach the microbench. ping me if you want quick pair to interpret perfetto.
mira: :thumbsup: will follow up with the 6h canary output and summary numbers.
